transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Um, thank you so much for seeing me today. I really appreciate it. 

Well, I guess I came in because... um, people have been pointing out some things about how I'm acting lately. I hope it's okay to start with that? It's kind of embarrassing, honestly, but they can actually see me doing these things. Sometimes I guess I'm moving like I'm underwater. Like, it takes me forever just to answer a question or even push myself out of a chair. I don't mean to be difficult or slow, I just... I don't know, it just happens. 

But then other times, I'm doing the exact opposite. I'll just be pacing around my apartment, rubbing my hands together over and over, kind of like I'm trying to shake off a really bad customer service call at work. It's probably not a huge deal, but since people were noticing, I figured I should be responsible and get it checked out. Does... does that make sense? Is that the kind of information you need?
Have you experienced any periods where your mood felt unusually high, elated, or irritable for several days in a row?

Oh, um, no, I don't think so. I really try my best not to be irritable with anyone. You know, working in customer service, you kind of have to learn to keep a smile on and not let things get to you, so I definitely haven't had days in a row of being snappy or angry. 

And I wouldn't say I've felt elated or unusually high, either. I mean, I wish I felt a little more upbeat sometimes, but... no, nothing extreme like what you're describing. 

Is it okay that I haven't experienced that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers. Am I doing alright so far?
Have you ever had a period of time where your mood was consistently elevated, irritable, or you felt unusually energetic, even if it was just for a few days?

Um, no, I... I really don't think so. I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm understanding you correctly. 

I haven't had any days where I felt super energetic or elevated. Honestly, most of the time I'm just trying to keep up with everything at work and not let anyone down. I definitely don't have periods where I'm irritable or anything like that. I always try to be as patient and polite as I can be, even when things are stressful. 

I hope that's okay? I just... I haven't noticed anything like that. Am I answering your questions the way you need me to?
Have you been feeling down or having a low mood most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Um, well... I guess I wouldn't say I've been feeling down *every* day. I mean, everyone gets a little sad sometimes, right? Especially when work gets overwhelming or, you know, when you feel like you aren't doing a good enough job. 

I try really hard to stay positive. I always make sure to smile when I'm on the phone with customers, and I try to keep my chin up. I don't want to be a burden on anyone or bring the mood down. So, no, I wouldn't say it's been most of the day, nearly every day. Just... normal ups and downs, I think. 

I hope that makes sense? I just don't want to make it sound worse than it is. Is that the kind of answer you were looking for?
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you normally like doing?

Um... well, I guess maybe a little bit? But I think it's just because I've been so tired from work, you know? 

Like, I used to really love sketching, and I'd always take these little notes when I tried different coffees, or I'd go for hikes on the weekends. They always made me feel really grounded, like myself. But lately... I don't know, I'll open my notebook or get my hiking boots out, and I just... I don't feel that same pull to actually do it. It just feels like a lot of effort right now. 

But I'm sure it's just a temporary thing, right? Like I just need to catch up on my sleep and then I'll be back to normal. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around doing nothing all the time. I still try to keep busy. Is it normal to go through phases like that where you just need a break from your hobbies?
Can you think back over the last few months—was there ever a time when you felt down or low for two weeks or more, even if it has since improved?

Um, well... let me think. The last few months have just been a blur of work, mostly. I mean, I definitely wouldn't say I was stuck feeling low for two whole weeks straight. That sounds... really intense, you know? 

I might have had a few days here and there where I was just feeling a bit run down or maybe a little quiet, but I always pushed through it. I make sure to show up to my shifts and do my best, so I wouldn't let myself just stay down like that for weeks. I think everyone gets a little stressed and tired sometimes, right? 

I really hope I'm being helpful. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information. I haven't had any big, long stretches like that, though. Does that make sense?
Have other people ever mentioned that your movements or speech seem unusually slow or, on the flip side, unusually restless or agitated, even when you yourself might not have noticed it?

Um... well, I guess someone has brought it up before, but I really don't think it's as bad as it sounds. Like, a couple of people have joked that sometimes I move like I’m underwater? Just taking forever to answer a question, or being really slow to get out of a chair. But I think I'm just being thoughtful, you know? I don't want to rush and say the wrong thing. 

And then... well, sometimes it's kind of the opposite. My roommate mentioned that I’ll be pacing around the apartment, just walking back and forth and rubbing my hands together. But I told him it's just because of work! When you get a really difficult customer, sometimes you just feel like you have to physically shake off a bad call, right? It's just a way to burn off the stress so I don't bother anyone with a bad mood. 

I really try to keep it under control so I don't make anyone uncomfortable. Is that... is that the sort of thing you meant? I hope I'm answering this right, I just don't want you to think I'm acting totally out of control or anything.

Can you recall if there was ever a time when you felt down, low, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row—even if that time was in the past and you feel better now?

Um... well, no, I really don't think so. I know you asked something similar before, and I... I hope it's okay that my answer is still the same. I just really haven't had a time where I felt hopeless or down like that for two whole weeks. 

I mean, sure, I get sad sometimes, just like anybody else. Like if I have a really rough day on the phones or if I'm just exhausted. But it never lasts that long, and I always try to look on the bright side, you know? I really make an effort not to let myself get stuck in a bad headspace because I want to be pleasant to be around. 

I don't want to sound like I'm not taking your questions seriously, I promise I am. I just... I haven't experienced that deep, constant hopelessness you're describing. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture.
How long have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you normally like doing?

Um... well, I suppose it's been happening a little bit lately, but I really don't want to make it sound like a huge problem. It's probably just normal tiredness from my shifts, you know? 

Like, I usually love sketching, or keeping these little notes on different coffees I try, and going on weekend hikes. Those things always used to make me feel... well, really like myself, I guess. But lately, maybe for the last couple of weeks or so, I'll open my notebook or lace up my hiking boots, and... I don't know, I just feel kind of nothing pulling me toward it? I just look at them and end up putting them away. 

But I'm sure it's just a temporary phase! I mean, everyone gets a little burned out and needs a break from their hobbies sometimes, right? I really hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. Does that make sense for what you're asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of examples.
Can you think back to any specific time in the past few months when you felt down, low, or without hope for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

Um... well, honestly, I still don't think I've had a time like that. I know you're asking about the past few months now, and I really am trying to think back carefully because I want to give you the right information. 

I mean, work has been stressful, and I've had days where I felt a little drained or bummed out after a bad shift. But it's never been, like, every single day for two whole weeks, and I definitely wouldn't say I felt hopeless. I always try to keep a positive attitude, you know? I don't want to be one of those people who just complains all the time or brings everyone else down. 

I really hope it's okay that my answer is still no. I'm not trying to be difficult or avoid the question, I promise. I just... I haven't felt that kind of constant low. Is it alright that I don't have an example like that for you? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
Have you ever had a time when you felt unusually irritable or your mood was elevated for at least four consecutive days, even if it wasn’t long enough to be considered a full episode?

Um... no, I really don't think so. I've never really been the type to get super irritable or, you know, overly hyper like that. 

I mean, if I have a lot of customers yelling at me on the phone, I might get a little frustrated for a minute, but I always try to brush it off and keep a smile in my voice. It's just part of the job, right? And I definitely wouldn't say I've ever felt unusually elevated or anything for days at a time. I try to keep pretty even-keeled so I'm easy to work with. 

I hope that's okay? I know you're trying to figure everything out, and I really want to be helpful. I just haven't experienced anything like that. Is that the kind of answer you were looking for?
Have you had days where your mood felt persistently low for most of the day, and this happened on most days for at least two weeks in a row?

Um... well, I know we just talked about this a little bit, and I really don't want to sound like a broken record, but... no, I really haven't. 

I mean, I'm trying to think really hard because I know you're asking it again, maybe in a slightly different way? But I just haven't had that feeling of being down for most of the day, every day, for two weeks straight. I really try to stay positive and not let things get to me too much. I'd hate to be a burden on anyone by being gloomy all the time. 

I really hope I'm not messing up the interview by not having a better answer for you. I just want to be completely honest. Is it okay that my answer is still no? I'm trying my best to give you what you need.
Can you think back to any time in the past few months when you felt down or low on most days for a period of at least two weeks in a row?

Um... well... I know I kept saying no before, and I really, really hope you're not frustrated with me. I wasn't trying to be difficult, I promise. I just... I hate complaining, and I always want to seem like I'm handling things okay. 

But... I guess if I'm being completely honest, maybe I have been. It's just that it doesn't feel like this big dramatic thing, it's more like... like it's just always there in the background? Most of the time since all this started, there's just been this... this sadness, and feeling kind of guilty, and not really having much interest in things. And my sleep has been pretty off, too. 

But it's mostly just background noise, you know? Like, some weeks are definitely lighter than others, and I still go to work and put on a brave face for the customers. I just push through it so I'm not bothering anyone. Is... is that what you meant? I'm so sorry I didn't just explain it like that the first time, I just didn't want to sound like I was whining.
Can you describe how many days out of the week, and for how many weeks in a row, you felt that background sadness or low mood was present?

Um... well, it's... it's been a really long time, actually. I hope that's okay to say. I just didn't want to make a big deal out of it before. 

If I really think about it, that background feeling... it's been there for about two years and maybe a month? It's not like I'm crying every single day or anything dramatic like that. There are definitely little brief periods where it eases up a bit and I feel a little lighter, especially if work is going well and I'm helping people. But mostly, it's just kind of... there. Most days of the week, for all those weeks. 

I just try really hard to keep it tucked away so I can still be pleasant for everyone else. I hope I'm answering this right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline so you can do your job. Is that the kind of detail you needed?
So you mentioned the background sadness has been there for about two years — can you confirm if that low mood was present for most of the day, on most days, during that time?

Oh... um, I really don't want to exaggerate and make it sound worse than it actually is. I'm sorry if I gave the wrong impression just now. 

I mean... I wouldn't say it's *most* of the day. When I'm at work, you know, talking to customers and staying busy, I'm really focused on them. I put on my customer service smile and I'm not really feeling that sadness during those hours because I'm trying to be helpful. So it's definitely not the whole day, or even most of it, I don't think? It's more just... when I have downtime, or when I finally get home and the house is quiet. 

I really hope I'm not being too confusing by changing my answer a little. I just want to make sure I'm being perfectly accurate so I don't mess up your notes or make you think I'm doing worse than I am. Is it okay that it's not most of the day? I'm really trying to get this right for you.
So to be clear, even if it's not the whole day, have you had a low or sad mood that's been present more days than not for the past two years?

Um... yeah, I guess so. I mean, I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining, but... yes. More days than not. 

It's just that, like I was trying to say earlier, it's not this overwhelming, terrible thing all the time. Most of the time since all this started, the... the sadness, and feeling bad about myself—the guilt, I guess—and just not really caring about my hobbies as much... and the sleep stuff... it's all just been there in the background. Even if some weeks are definitely lighter than others, and I feel a bit better, it's still kind of lingering underneath. 

I just... I hope I'm making sense. I know I keep going back and forth on how bad it is, and I really don't want to frustrate you. I just want to make sure you understand that I'm still trying my best to function and not let it ruin everything. Does that... does that answer your question better?
